title: Your First Family Camping Trip: A Beginner’s Checklist
description: Planning your first family camping trip? Choosing a campsite, what kit you really need, cooking, keeping kids warm at night and a practice run in the garden.
intro: Marshmallows, torch-lit tents and waking up outdoors. Camping is a cheap, brilliant adventure, and a bit of prep makes the first trip a happy one.

image.alt: A family walking together on a grassy hill

cardText: Campsites, kit, cooking and keeping warm at night.

blocks.title: Scout’s camping tip
blocks.text: Do a practice night in the garden first. You’ll find out what’s missing, and whether everyone actually likes it, without a long drive home.
points: Pick a campsite with good facilities first time
Nights get cold, even in summer

sections.html: For a first trip, choose a site with toilets, showers and a play area, not too far from home. Check whether it allows campfires, and how far the car park is from your pitch.

• A tent you’ve practised putting up.
  • Warm sleeping bags rated for the season, plus mats or airbeds.
  • Head torches for everyone.
  • A simple stove, pans and a cool box.
  • Layers, waterproofs and wellies.
Try glamping first: beds, sometimes electricity, all the fun. Plan days out from the site with the adventure finder.

faqs.q: What age can kids go camping?
faqs.a: Families camp with children of all ages, including babies. Choose sites with good facilities and plan for cold nights.
